scenes.headline: 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo
scenes.narration: A masterpiece in automotive history, the 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo blends iconic design with sheer power. This 3.6-liter twin-turbo flat-six engine pushes 400 horsepower, making it a legend among sports cars.

scenes.headline: Legacy of Speed
scenes.narration: Introduced in 1995, this generation was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, enhancing grip and stability.

scenes.headline: Value: $110K -> $70K
scenes.narration: Originally priced around $110,000, a '96 model trades for about $70,000 today, reflecting a stable value in the classic car market.

scenes.headline: Wide Body Performance
scenes.narration: The wide rear body design with prominent fender arches improves both aerodynamics and grip.

scenes.headline: Twin-Turbo Performance
scenes.narration: Under the hood sits an air-cooled 3.6-liter engine, backed by an air-to-air intercooler.

scenes.headline: Driver-Focused Design
scenes.narration: The interior of the 911 Turbo isn't just about luxury; it features a prominent analog gauge cluster with five dials and that reassuring classic feel.

scenes.headline: The Final Air-Cooled Turbo
scenes.narration: As the last air-cooled 911 Turbo, this model holds a special place in Porsche history.

scenes.headline: Cooling Details
scenes.narration: The prominent air-to-oil cooler in this 911 Turbo ensures efficient heat dissipation.

scenes.headline: Unanswered Potential
scenes.narration: So, would you choose the 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo for its iconic status and groundbreaking engineering?

script: A masterpiece in automotive history, the 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo blends iconic design with sheer power. This 3.6-liter twin-turbo flat-six engine pushes 400 horsepower, making it a legend among sports cars. Introduced in 1995, this generation was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, enhancing grip and stability. Originally priced around $110,000, a '96 model trades for about $70,000 today, reflecting a stable value in the classic car market. The wide rear body design with prominent fender arches improves both aerodynamics and grip. Under the hood sits an air-cooled 3.6-liter engine, backed by an air-to-air intercooler. The interior of the 911 Turbo isn't just about luxury; it features a prominent analog gauge cluster with five dials and that reassuring classic feel. As the last air-cooled 911 Turbo, this model holds a special place in Porsche history. The prominent air-to-oil cooler in this 911 Turbo ensures efficient heat dissipation. So, would you choose the 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo for its iconic status and groundbreaking engineering?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo, finished in Arena Red Metallic with a black interior. This 911 Turbo is owned by journalist and Cars & Bids founder Doug DeMuro, and associated videos are viewable below. This Porsche is equipped with a 6-speed manual transmission, and the odometer currently displays approximately 62,800 miles. This 993 is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report, and it has reportedly been registered in California since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels, a limited-slip differential, a sunroof, supple leather upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, and air conditioning. Notable modifications reported by the seller are limited to a Porsche Classic Communication Management (PCCM) head unit. Documentation of maintenance and repairs performed is extensive and reportedly dates back to new. Recent highlights include a $24,470 service in February 2026 that included replacing the valve covers, timing chain covers, crankshaft seal, turbo oil feed lines, and more, as detailed by documentation in the gallery. The 993-generation 911 Turbo, introduced in 1995, was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, providing enhanced traction and stability. Its twin-turbocharged flat-6 engine, distinctive wide-body design, and status as the final air-cooled Porsche have made it a favorite among Porsche enthusiasts -- and Arena Red Metallic remains one of the most famous 993 Turbo colors thanks to the iconic "Kills Bugs Fast" advertisement. Power comes from a 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged flat-6, rated at 400 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque. Power is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
sections.Equipment: A window sticker is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels Xenon headlights Power-operated sunroof Rear wiper Supple leather upholstery Power-adjustable front seats Air conditioning Cruise control
sections.Seller Notes: The seller reports that some touch-up paintwork has been performed on forward-facing surfaces at some point in the past, and a full-body paint protection film and a ceramic coating have since been applied to this 911 Turbo.
